title: Keeping a Fragile Peace
text:
Peacekeeping is one of the least understood roles of modern armed forces. When people imagine soldiers, they usually picture combat. Peacekeepers, however, are sent to areas where a conflict has stopped, or is supposed to have stopped, and their task is to help the peace hold. Since the first major United Nations peacekeeping missions in the mid-twentieth century, many thousands of military personnel from dozens of countries, including Brazil, have served in such operations around the world.

Traditional peacekeeping was based on a few key principles. Missions were deployed only with the consent of the parties to the conflict; peacekeepers were expected to be impartial, treating all sides equally; and they were allowed to use force only in self-defence. Their typical tasks included monitoring ceasefires, patrolling buffer zones between opposing forces and reporting violations.

Over time, the role has become more complex. Many recent conflicts have taken place within countries rather than between them, involving armed groups that do not always respect agreements. Peacekeeping missions have therefore been given broader mandates: protecting civilians, supporting elections, helping to disarm former fighters and assisting in the reconstruction of institutions such as the police and the courts. In some cases, peacekeepers have been authorised to use force more actively to protect people under threat.

This expansion has brought new challenges. Peacekeepers must often operate in vast territories with limited resources, and they may be seen as enemies by groups that oppose the peace process. They must work closely with civilian organisations, humanitarian agencies and local communities, which requires skills that are not always part of traditional military training: negotiation, cultural awareness and the ability to communicate with people who may have good reasons to distrust anyone in uniform.

The record of peacekeeping is mixed. There have been notable failures, in which missions were unable to prevent terrible violence against civilians, and cases of misconduct by peacekeepers that seriously damaged trust. At the same time, studies suggest that, on average, the presence of peacekeepers reduces the likelihood that a conflict will start again, and many countries that hosted missions have gone on to enjoy long periods of relative stability.

For the soldiers involved, peacekeeping can be a profoundly formative experience. Many describe the challenge of maintaining discipline and restraint in tense situations as more demanding than they had expected. As one officer put it, "In combat, the objective is clear. In peacekeeping, every day you have to decide what the right thing to do is."

questions.prompt: What is the main task of peacekeepers, according to paragraph 1?
options: To help a peace that has been agreed to last
To train the armies of other countries
questions.explanation: “their task is to help the peace hold”.

questions.prompt: Which was NOT a principle of traditional peacekeeping?
options: Missions needed the consent of the parties.
Peacekeepers could attack armed groups whenever necessary.
Force could be used only in self-defence.
questions.explanation: Force was allowed only in self-defence.

questions.prompt: The word “impartial” in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to
Why have peacekeeping mandates become broader?
options: Many recent conflicts are within countries and involve armed groups that ignore agreements.
The United Nations has stopped traditional missions.

questions.prompt: Which skill does the author say is not always part of traditional military training?
questions.explanation: “negotiation, cultural awareness and the ability to communicate”.

questions.prompt: Why might local people distrust peacekeepers?
options: Peacekeepers do not speak to civilians.
They may have good reasons to distrust anyone in uniform.
Peacekeepers are not allowed to help civilians.

questions.prompt: How does the author describe the record of peacekeeping?
options: It has been a complete success.
It includes both failures and successes.
It has been a complete failure.

questions.prompt: According to studies mentioned in paragraph 5, peacekeepers
options: reduce the likelihood that a conflict will start again

questions.prompt: What does the officer suggest in the last sentence?
options: Combat is more difficult than peacekeeping.
Peacekeepers do not need clear orders.
